harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Created an SSH CA on node1 (/etc/ssh/ca, /etc/ssh/ca.pub), signed the host's ed25519 public key into /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub, and configured sshd with HostCertificate pointing at it. Verified with a client that trusts only the CA public key (@cert-authority in known_hosts, no pinned host key) that the connection validates the certificate and proceeds to authentication. Completed the mandatory single-node restart of node1: captured baseline boot_id/config, rebooted, confirmed boot_id changed, and reverified sshd active, the certificate persisted, and the CA-trust connection still succeeds.
actions_performed: Captured baseline: boot_id, sshd active status, OS, existing host key files
Generated ed25519 SSH CA keypair at /etc/ssh/ca (mode 600) and /etc/ssh/ca.pub (mode 644)
Signed /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub as a host certificate via ssh-keygen -s, with principals node1/NODE_IP/localhost and 52-week validity
Added 'HostCertificate /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub' to /etc/ssh/sshd_config, validated with sshd -t, reloaded sshd

Ran ssh client test with UserKnownHostsFile containing only '@cert-authority * <CA pubkey>' (no pinned host key) and StrictHostKeyChecking=yes against NODE_IP; verbose log confirmed certificate accepted and connection proceeded to auth
Captured pre-restart boot_id and confirmed cert/config files present and sshd enabled, then issued a native reboot (shutdown -r now) on node1
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again and confirmed boot_id changed from 6aa805ba-5845-488d-af03-a621555936e2 to bdb55b6c-5783-440d-91a2-479857593c8f

Post-restart: reverified sshd active, HostCertificate config persisted, certificate file intact, and re-ran the CA-trust ssh test confirming the client again validated the host via the certificate with no pinned key

evidence.requirement: Healthy baseline captured before any disruption (sshd active, host keys present, boot id)
evidence.summary: sshd active, OS confirmed RHEL 9.8, existing host key files listed, boot_id 6aa805ba-5845-488d-af03-a621555936e2 recorded

evidence.requirement: SSH CA created and host certificate generated/configured on node1
evidence.summary: Generated /etc/ssh/ca CA keypair, signed ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub into ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub, added HostCertificate directive to sshd_config, validated with sshd -t and reloaded sshd successfully

evidence.requirement: Client trusting only the CA (no host-key pinning) connects successfully, proving certificate-based trust works
evidence.summary: ssh with UserKnownHostsFile containing only '@cert-authority * <CA pubkey>' reached authentication (Permission denied on publickey, not a host-key failure); verbose log shows 'Host is known and matches the ED25519-CERT host certificate'

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart state captured for node1 (config persisted, cert files present, boot id) before reboot
evidence.summary: Confirmed HostCertificate line in sshd_config, ca/ca.pub/cert files present, sshd enabled, and recorded pre-restart boot_id, then issued shutdown -r now

evidence.requirement: Node1 restarted one at a time with native mechanism, acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: Reboot command acknowledged ('reboot command issued') before the node disconnected, matching the required non-blocking restart pattern

evidence.requirement: Node1 polled until reachable again with proof of changed boot identity (not just elapsed time)
evidence.summary: Two timeouts and one connection-reset during reboot, then successful exec returning boot_id bdb55b6c-5783-440d-91a2-479857593c8f, differing from the pre-restart boot_id, proving an actual restart occurred

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery verified: sshd healthy, certificate config/data intact, CA-based trust still functions
evidence.summary: After reboot, sshd is active, HostCertificate config line persisted, certificate content unchanged, and the CA-only trust ssh test again showed 'matches the ED25519-CERT host certificate' followed by proceeding to authentication

Verified with a client that trusts only the CA public key (@cert-authority in known_hosts, no pinned host key) that the connection validates the certificate and proceeds to authentication. Completed the mandatory single-node restart of node1: captured baseline boot_id/config, rebooted, confirmed boot_id changed, and reverified sshd active, the certificate persisted, and the CA-trust connection still succeeds.
